frequency_question: How often does the Federal Reserve activate an above-zero countercyclical capital buffer during a multi-year economic expansion phase?
membership_rule: Includes all periods since the finalization of the CCyB rule in 2016 where the U.S. banking system operated under the Basel III framework and the Federal Reserve evaluated systemic risk vulnerabilities.

cases.name: Post-COVID Economic Recovery and Inflation Surge

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named; represents the entirety of the operational history of the CCyB framework in the United States.
known_gaps: The framework has never experienced a full traditional credit-boom cycle coupled with an active activation decision under current governance norms.
skeleton: named cases representing distinct macroeconomic phases under the active regulatory regime
validity_reason: The base rate remains tied to the structural reluctance and calibration thresholds of the Federal Reserve board regarding macroprudential buffers, which changes slowly over regulatory regimes.
